description.narrative: RECONOMY for the Eastern Partnership (EaP) Region is a regional program with the objective "Women and youth, in particular, disadvantaged and excluded groups, benefit from improved economic opportunities (better income and decent and green jobs) inclusively and sustainably". The program uses a Market Systems Development Approach. This approach underlines the importance of systemic change: understanding where market systems are failing to serve the needs of people living in poverty, and acting to correct those failings, mainly by creating incentives among the actors in the system to make the system more inclusive. MSD promotes, among other things locally adapted and innovative solutions, adaptive programming and sustainable results at scale. This program is one of two “sub-programs” in one regional program covering both the Eastern Partnership and Western Balkans. Both sub-programs have country windows, one in EaP, Armenia, and one in WB, North Macedonia. Employment and income increases for excluded groups are a key component of inclusive economic development worldwide. In Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans, local welfare is negatively affected by both poverty, brain drain and discrimination against different population groups. Income and employment for development cooperation's target groups counteract these negative trends. In a sensitive transition process from central government to more open economies, the continued willingness to reform is also strongly influenced by the perceived gains from already implemented changes. To stay competitive in global markets, development towards green transition is necessary and therefore also green skills and adapted business models. The program is implemented by Helvetas, a Swiss NGO with experience from working with market system development. RECONOMY is an innovative program in that it uses an MSD approach at the regional level. Often the "Markets" in MSD approaches are limited by national borders. But especially in the Eastern Partnership and in the Western Balkans, this is rarely the case. Various aspects of the market systems cross borders and RECONOMY has a well-developed way of exploiting these opportunities for development. The approach includes: • Common problems – where similar issues exist in different contexts and lessons from one context can be applied in another. • Shared problems – where trade in goods, services, information or other cross borders and present a particular challenge or opportunity and which RECONOMY can address. • Shared solutions – where RECONOMY utilizes knowledge and networks within several related markets to work with the same private sector actors or administrative actors in several countries.

RECONOMY för Östra Partnerskapet (Eastern Partnership (EaP) Region) är ett regionalt program med målet "Kvinnor och ungdomar, i synnerhet från missgynnade och utestängda grupper, drar nytta av förbättrade ekonomiska möjligheter (bättre inkomst och anständiga och gröna jobb) på ett inkluderande och hållbart sätt". Programmet bygger på en marknadssystemansats (MSD). Detta innebär ett fokus på systemförändringar. Inom programmet byggs en förståelse för var marknadssystem misslyckas med att tillgodose behoven hos människor som lever i fattigdom. Programmet inriktas på att rätta till dessa brister, främst genom att skapa incitament bland aktörerna i systemet för att göra systemet mer inkluderande. MSD främjar bland annat lokalt anpassade och innovativa lösningar, adaptiv programmering och hållbara resultat i stor skala. Detta program är ett av två ”del-program” i ett regionalt program som täcker både Östra Partnerskapet och Västra Balkan. Båda del-programmen har var sitt landfönster, ett i EaP, Armenien, och ett i VB, Nordmakedonien. Sysselsättning och inkomstökningar för exkluderade grupper är en nyckelkomponent av inkluderande ekonomisk utveckling i hela världen. I Östeuropa och på Västra Balkan påverkas samhället negativt av både fattigdom, kompetensflykt och diskriminering av olika befolkningsgrupper. Inkomster och sysselsättning för utvecklingssamarbetets målgrupper motverkar dessa negativa trender. I en känslig transitionsprocess från centralstyre till mer öppna ekonomier påverkas den fortsatta reformviljan också starkt av de upplevda vinsterna från redan genomförda förändringar. För att vara konkurrenskraftig i globala marknader krävs en utveckling mot en grön omställning och därmed även nya kompetenser och nya anpassade affärsmodeller. Programmet genomförs av Helvetas, en schweizisk NGO med erfarenhet av att arbeta med MSD-metoden. RECONOMY är ett innovativt program genom att det använder MSD på regional nivå. Ofta begränsas "Marknaderna" i MSD-ansatser av nationella gränser. Men särskilt i det Östliga Partnerskapet och på Västra Balkan är det sällan fallet. Olika aspekter av marknadssystemen sträcker sig över gränserna och RECONOMY har ett välutvecklat sätt att utnyttja dessa möjligheter till utveckling. Tillvägagångssättet inkluderar: • Gemensamma problem – där liknande frågor finns i olika sammanhang och lärdomar från ett sammanhang kan vara tillämpas i ett annat. • Delade problem – där handel med varor, tjänster, information eller annat korsar gränser och innebär en speciell utmaning eller möjlighet och som RECONOMY kan adressera. • Delade lösningar – där RECONOMY utnyttjar kunskaper och nätverk inom flera relaterade marknader för att arbeta med samma näringslivsaktörer eller förvaltningsaktörer i flera länder.

The original objective of RECONOMY (December, 2022) is:
Women and youth, including the most disadvantaged and excluded, benefit from improved economic opportunities (better income and decent and green jobs) inclusively and sustainably.
By the end of the project it is expected that a number of women and youth have got additional income and decent and green job opportunities. (Target 28,750 women and youth of which at least 50% are women and at least 10% from the most disadvantaged and excluded groups, at least 30% green jobs). It is further expected that:
The amount of additional investment made by private sector enterprises increase because of changes stimulated by the program (target: CHF 20,000,000.00, CHF 5,000,000 green finance)
A percentage of private sector enterprises that report higher turnover and/or profit as a result of changes stimulated by the program (target: 40%)
Increased number of women and youth with improved skills relevant to market needs (target: 20,000 women and youth, at least 50% women, at least 10% of the most disadvantaged and excluded, at least 30% green skills)
Number of women and youth that access and use intermediation services (target: 100,000, 10% disadvantaged and excluded groups)
Number of private sector enterprises report better performance as a result of clear and implemented policies/regulations/administrative requirements as a result of the programs facilitation (target: 1100, disaggregated by services and sectors)
A percentage of private sector enterprises that report increased economic opportunities and business environment (target: 40%)

Progress during 2023 was primarily visible in the area of programme establishment. A Programme Facilitation Unit (PFU) team of 23 people was hired and four implementing partners were procured. Nine market systems analyses were conducted across the eleven countries in the two regions (five in EaP countries and six in Western Balkans), leading to the creation of 22 intervention guides for eight projects. The interventions are building on research and results of pilot projects implemented during the inception phase, meanwhile the original research is updated in collaboration with newly selected implementing partners and sharpened in line with RECONOMY's over-arching priority themes for full-scale implementation: Green transformation and digitalization.
Over the year, agreements were signed with 35 market actors who committed to co-invest in various initiatives.
During the first half of 2024, over-arching results have been reported for EaP and Armenia in the following areas:
- 2,852 women and youth benefited from improved employment opportunities stimulated by the programme, 1,261 young men and 1,591 women, 838 were from the most excluded groups and 284 of those employment opportunities were classified as "green jobs"
- Out of the regional results for employment opportunities stimulated by the programme, a remarkable share of 2,500 were recorded for the Armenia country window
- In total, approximately 117,764 individuals were reached through various activities (2,000 physical and 115,764 online). Direct training and development were provided to 775 participants from the target group. The program engaged with 1,062 private sector companies, with the potential to impact an estimated 15,147 employees and securing CHF 294,902 in private sector investment, including in-kind contributions from Market Actors (MAs), financial investments, and other types of support.
